We work with clients across real estate, technology, banking and finance, and employment, among other sectors. Whatever industry you're in, we've likely handled something similar before.

company-incorporation.title: Company Setup & KSA Market Entry Lawyers
company-incorporation.intro: Northman Sterling Legal guides foreign investors through every stage of Saudi market entry — MISA licensing, entity structuring, and full company incorporation — so your business is registered, licensed, and compliant from day one.

sections.heading: MISA Licensing & Market Entry Strategy
sections.body: Before any Saudi entity can be formed, most foreign-owned businesses need a license from the Ministry of Investment of Saudi Arabia (MISA). We assess which license category fits your activity, prepare and submit the MISA application, and advise on the market entry structure that best matches your commercial goals — full incorporation, a branch, or a representative office.
items: MISA license category assessment and application
Foreign ownership rules by sector and activity
Market entry strategy: subsidiary, branch, or representative office

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Legal Entity
sections.body: Saudi Arabia offers several legal entity forms, and the right choice depends on your shareholding structure, capital, and commercial activity. A Limited Liability Company (LLC) is the most common vehicle for foreign investors, offering limited liability with capital requirements set by MISA based on activity. A Branch of a Foreign Company allows 100% foreign ownership without a local sponsor, but the parent company bears full liability and branches cannot engage in trading. A Joint Stock Company (JSC) suits larger multinational investors or businesses planning a future listing, with higher minimum capital requirements. We advise on which structure fits your investment before you commit to one.
items: Limited Liability Company (LLC) — the standard vehicle for most foreign investors
Branch of a Foreign Company — 100% foreign ownership, no local sponsor required
Joint Stock Company (JSC) — for larger or listing-track investors
Representative office, technical/scientific services office, and other specialized forms

sections.heading: Incorporation, Registration & Post-Formation Compliance
sections.body: Once the entity structure is set, we manage the full registration process — name reservation, MISA license approval, notarizing the Articles of Association, obtaining the Commercial Registration, and registering with the Chamber of Commerce, GOSI (social insurance), the Ministry of Human Resources, and ZATCA for tax purposes. We also support opening a corporate bank account and staying compliant with annual reporting, auditor appointment, and license renewal obligations after formation.
items: Commercial Registration and Articles of Association
GOSI, labor, and Chamber of Commerce registration
ZATCA tax registration and ongoing compliance

sections.body: We advise lenders and borrowers on structuring, negotiating, and documenting financing transactions, including corporate loans, project finance, and syndicated facilities in the Saudi market.

sections.heading: Islamic (Shariah-Compliant) Finance
sections.body: We structure Shariah-compliant financing arrangements, including Murabaha, Ijara, and Sukuk-based structures, for clients seeking financing that complies with Islamic finance principles alongside conventional facilities.

sections.heading: SAMA Regulatory Compliance
sections.body: We advise banks and financial institutions on compliance with Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) regulations, licensing requirements, and prudential obligations relevant to their Saudi operations.

highlights.title: Conventional & Islamic Finance
highlights.description: Experience structuring both conventional and Shariah-compliant financing.

highlights.title: SAMA-Aware

highlights.title: Lender & Borrower Experience

capital-markets.title: Capital Markets Lawyers in Saudi Arabia
capital-markets.intro: We advise issuers, underwriters, and investors on IPOs, debt issuances, and other capital markets transactions regulated by the Capital Market Authority (CMA) and Saudi Exchange (Tadawul).

sections.heading: IPOs & Equity Offerings
sections.body: We advise companies and underwriters on initial public offerings and equity capital raises on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul), including prospectus preparation, CMA approvals, and listing requirements.

sections.heading: Debt Capital Markets
sections.body: We advise on debt issuances, including bonds and Sukuk, structuring offerings that comply with CMA regulations and meet the requirements of institutional and retail investors.

sections.heading: CMA Regulatory Advisory
sections.body: We advise listed companies and market participants on ongoing compliance with CMA rules, corporate governance requirements, and disclosure obligations under Saudi securities regulation.

highlights.title: CMA & Tadawul Experience
highlights.description: Direct familiarity with Saudi Arabia's capital markets regulator and exchange.

highlights.title: Issuer & Underwriter Side
highlights.description: Advisory experience from both the issuer and underwriter perspective.

highlights.title: Governance-Focused
highlights.description: Ongoing compliance support, not just one-time transaction advice.

termsAndConditions.title: Terms and Conditions
termsAndConditions.intro: These terms and conditions ("Agreement") govern the use of legal advisory and related services offered by Northman Sterling Legal. By engaging with our services, you agree to comply with these terms and conditions in their entirety.

sections.heading: Scope of Services
sections.body: Northman Sterling Legal offers professional legal advisory services to corporates and businesses operating in or entering Saudi Arabia. Our services include but are not limited to corporate and commercial advisory, dispute resolution, regulatory compliance, notary and Power of Attorney issuance, and related legal support.

sections.heading: Client Obligations
sections.body: As a client of Northman Sterling Legal, you agree to provide accurate and complete information regarding your matter. It is your responsibility to ensure the authenticity and validity of all provided documents. Any false or misleading information may result in the termination of our services without liability.

sections.heading: Service Fees and Payment
sections.body: Northman Sterling Legal's service fees are disclosed prior to engagement and are based on the specific services requested. All fees quoted are exclusive of any government charges, taxes, or third-party expenses. Payment terms and methods will be discussed and agreed upon with the client. Failure to make timely payments may result in a suspension or termination of services.

sections.heading: Confidentiality
sections.body: We understand the sensitivity of client information and ensure the highest level of confidentiality. We undertake to handle all client data and documents with strict confidentiality, except as required by law or with the client's consent.

sections.heading: Limitation of Liability
sections.body: Northman Sterling Legal will exercise reasonable care and skill in delivering its services. However, we do not guarantee the outcome of any specific legal matter, as the final decision on many matters lies with the relevant Saudi courts or authorities. We shall not be liable for any direct, indirect, or consequential damages arising from the use or inability to use our services.

sections.heading: Termination of Services
sections.body: Either party may terminate the services by providing written notice to the other party. In the event of termination, any outstanding fees or expenses incurred up to the termination date will be due and payable.

You agree not to use, reproduce, or distribute any of our intellectual property without prior written consent.
